title: US equity markets close early at 1:00 p.m. ET — Christmas Eve
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes; the page needs curl -L, and its holiday data is JSON-ish '"text":"..."' cells rather than HTML table markup) and parsed cell-by-cell by this session. Its Christmas Day row parses as 'Friday, December 25****' for 2026, and footnote **** reads verbatim: 'Each market will close early at 1:00 p.m. (1:15 p.m. for eligible options) on Thursday, December 24, 2026. NYSE American Equities, NYSE Arca Equities, NYSE National, and NYSE Texas late trading sessions will close at 5:00 p.m. All times are Eastern Time.' Independently corroborated the same day by cboe.com/about/hours/us-options/ (HTTP 200, 387,220 bytes), whose 2026 table row reads 'Christmas Early Close | December 24 | 09:30:00 - 13:00:00'. Filed estimate rather than confirmed because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for an exchange operator's own hours page and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep.
notes: DISCOVERED during the thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), off the same NYSE fetch that sources this event's sibling. This is the entry the japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-12-25 lane found and then DELETED on 2026-09-05: its Honest limits record that it located the NYSE 2026-12-24 half-day as a dated primary-sourced adjacency but that scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs's KINDS list had 'no slot for a trading-hours event', so it declined to take a schema decision in passing. That decision has since been made in practice twice over — good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26 and thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 both carry a US trading-hours event as kind 'sector', impact low, symbols [], status estimate with a NEWS: source, and both validate clean. This entry reuses that precedent exactly; no new kind is invented. Why it earns a row on its own: it is the SECOND of only two NYSE early closes in 2026 and therefore the only comparison case for anything the thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 ledger concludes about half sessions — that ledger's measured claims (volume at a median 0.411x the trailing-20 session median; no ordinary Friday implied-vol crush) are stated for the day after Thanksgiving alone and have NOT been tested on Christmas Eve sessions. It is also the last US equity session before a full closure on Friday 2026-12-25, and it sits between cpi-2026-12-10 / the 2026-12-09 FOMC and the 2026-12-28 advance economic indicators report. Impact is LOW and symbols is empty: this is a market-structure fact that changes how other events are READ, not an event with its own directional content.
